<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/../src/Accessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/JsonAccessor.php';

use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\EnvAccessor;
use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\JsonAccessor;

$failures = 0;
function check(string $name, bool $ok): void
{
    global $failures;
    echo ($ok ? "ok   " : "FAIL ") . $name . "\n";
    if (!$ok) {
        $failures++;
    }
}

$env = new EnvAccessor("HOST=localhost\nPORT=3000\n");
check('reads KEY=value lines', $env->get('HOST') === 'localhost' && $env->get('PORT') === '3000');

$env = new EnvAccessor("# a comment\n\nKEY=value\n");
check('skips blank lines and comments', $env->all() === ['KEY' => 'value']);

$env = new EnvAccessor("A=\"one two\"\nB='three'\n");
check('strips one pair of matching quotes', $env->get('A') === 'one two' && $env->get('B') === 'three');

$env = new EnvAccessor('KEY=value');
check('answers the fallback for a key that is not there', $env->get('MISSING', 'none') === 'none' && $env->has('KEY') && !$env->has('MISSING'));

$json = new JsonAccessor('{"name":"x","count":3}');
check('json keeps the string values of an object', $json->all() === ['name' => 'x']);

exit($failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

content.text: Without the source change the two new tests fail in both packages. With it they pass. Now I'll record the one choice here that someone could question: how the `export` prefix is matched.

input.title: EnvAccessor drops a leading `export` followed by whitespace, before any other line check, in both packages
input.rationale: A line `export KEY=value` reads as `KEY=value`, exactly as if the prefix were not there. The prefix is matched as `^export\s+` on the trimmed line (JS `replace(/^export\s+/, '')`, PHP `preg_replace('/^export\s+/', '', ...)`), and it is removed first, before the blank-line, `#` comment and `=` checks, so everything after it follows the existing rules unchanged (quotes, trimming, comments). Any run of whitespace counts, since shell allows `export   KEY=v` and `export<TAB>KEY=v`. Because `export` must be followed by whitespace, a key that merely starts with it (`exported=b`, `export=a`) is untouched, and `export KEY` with no `=` is skipped like any other line without one. Made identically in packages/js and packages/php, as ADR-1 requires; the tests in both packages cover the prefix, the extra whitespace, and the non-prefix cases.
input.alternatives: Match the literal string `export ` (one space): rejected, `export<TAB>KEY=v` and aligned `export   KEY=v` are valid shell and would silently yield a key named `export   KEY`... or be skipped. Strip the prefix only after the comment and blank checks: rejected, `export # note` or `export #X=1` would then not read as the comment they are without the prefix, which breaks "exactly as if the prefix were not there". Parse shell syntax more fully (`declare -x`, `export -p`, multiple names per export, expansions): rejected, out of what was asked and against keeping the code plain with no dependencies.

content.text:
`EnvAccessor` now reads `export KEY=value` as `KEY=value`, in both packages. The JS and PHP suites pass (8 JS tests, all PHP checks).

I changed both packages because ADR-1 requires a behavior change in one to be made in the other in the same change. The fix is a single leading-`export` strip on the trimmed line in `packages/js/src/accessors/formats/env-accessor.ts` and `packages/php/src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php`.

- **Matching:** the prefix is `export` followed by whitespace, so `export   KEY=v` and `export<TAB>KEY=v` work. `exported=b` and `export=a` are left alone, and `export KEY` with no `=` is skipped like any other line without one.
- **Order:** the strip happens before the blank and `#` checks, so the prefix behaves as if it weren't there. For example, `export #X=1` is read as a comment.
- **Doc comments:** both class doc comments now mention the optional `export `.
- **Tests:** there are two new tests per package. One covers the prefix, extra whitespace, a quoted value and the plain-line mix. The other covers the non-prefix cases and the commented-out `export`. I stashed the source change to check them: both fail without it in both packages and pass with it.
- **Record:** I recorded the matching rule as ADR-2, with the alternatives I turned down (a literal single space, stripping after the comment check, and fuller shell parsing). It stays `proposed` until someone accepts it. It follows ADR-1 and doesn't replace it, so I left ADR-1 as it is.

I haven't committed anything. `git status` shows the four edited files plus new untracked files under `.mnema/`. Those are the ADR-2 record and a new signing key that the mnema hook created for this session. The hook said that key started an identity of its own beside the existing one (`mnid:3b2c3f61`). If that key is really you on another machine or key, the hook's message gives the `mnema key request --anchor mnid:3b2c3f61` steps to join it to your identity; otherwise there is nothing to do. When you commit, `.mnema/` should go in with the code.

One behavior change from before: `export = x` (the word `export` as a key, with spaces around `=`) used to give a key named `export`. It is now skipped, because it reads as `= x`. That follows from "exactly as if the prefix were not there", and I judged the case too unlikely to special-case.
